articles.headline: Prof. P. Houston Murray's Lectures
articles.author: P. Houston Murray
articles.summary: The young phrenologist, Prof. Murray, whose accuracy in delineating character has astonished all his magical fingers have come in contact with, after making a successful phrenological tour through Canada West and Western New York, has arrived in our city, and intends delivering a second lecture here during the coming week, of which the public will be duly notified. Any one wishing an oral examination, written, or a chart, can be accommodated by calling at his stopping-place, No. 14 Eutaw St. [VERIFY: printed form looks 'Eotaw'], where he will be pleased to accommodate them. articles.headline: Bishop's Allowance
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Philadelphia, June 30th, 1862. articles.headline: Rev. William Alston (preached at St. Thomas' Church)
articles.summary: Rev. William Alston, of New York, preached last Sabbath for St. Thomas' Church. We were present to hear our old North Carolina friend, and we were much pleased with his discourse. He read for his text: 'And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up.' ... When at Oberlin College, he and I boarded at the same house. The members of the St. Thomas' Church, we think, anticipate calling him for their minister.

articles.headline: Rev. Shepherd Holcomb
articles.summary: We have a letter from Rev. Shepherd Holcomb, of Mount Holly. Brother Holcomb, as many of our brethren are aware, is a superannuated minister, and all who know him, know him to be a man of piety. We are truly glad to learn from his letter that he has nearly recovered from the paralytics, and can move around.

articles.headline: Letter from Mount Holly (Shepherd Holcomb thanks the Female Aid Society)
articles.author: Shepherd Holcomb
articles.summary: Mount Holly, N. J., July 7, 1862. Mr. Editor: Please give this place in the Recorder this week. On the 6th of April last I was with Brother J. H. Smith holding Quarterly Meeting at Evesham [printed 'Eresham'], eight miles from my home, at which time I was taken with a paralytic stroke. I was brought home quite feeble, and the use of my left side entirely gone. It came under the notice of the Female Aid Society. Sister Mary Still, being a member of that Society, and knowing my condition, at once made it known to the Society, and through her influence they sent me three dollars by the hands of Sister Elizabeth Harris [VERIFY] of [Hu?]rntown [VERIFY], Pa.; and she gave me one dollar of her own private funds.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meeting, Rev. R. Roberson (Frankford)
articles.summary: There was a noble Quarterly Meeting held at Frankford. We were with Father Roberson on the occasion, and we had a blessed time indeed. articles.headline: Died: Gale (Boston; parents formerly of Philadelphia)
articles.summary: GALE.--Mr. Adam Gale, the son of Mr. James and Mrs. Elizabeth Gale, formerly of Philadelphia, departed this life in the city of Boston on the 7th instant, in the home of his affectionate parents, aged 22 years and 2 months. That slow but fatal disease, consumption, caused him to linger about five months. Dated Boston, Mass., July 14, 1862.

articles.headline: Notice (Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's illness)
articles.summary: Our much esteemed brother, Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, met with the sad misfortune of rupturing one of the blood vessels in his abdomen. On Tuesday, the 11th inst., he endured the painful process of a surgical operation. On Wednesday, the 12th inst., he was supposed to be better.

articles.headline: The War (editorial: enlistment of colored men for other States)
articles.summary: Another severe battle has been fought between Stonewall Jackson and General Banks, aided by General Pope, all under the command of General Halleck. ... We understand that there are movements on foot to have the colored people enlist to fill quotas, and send them out of this State to Rhode Island, under Governor Sprague, also to Kansas, under General Lane. We do not favor the project at all.

articles.headline: My Eastern Tour
articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Having promised to give, through your valuable paper, an account of my visit among those whom, I may say, are favored with the sublime appearance of a bright morning's sun at least 140 seconds earlier than we who reside in the city of Brotherly Love... my peculiar relation to the Wesley A. M. E. Church in this city has caused my delay to this late period. On Friday, the 11th ultimo, in company with Miss Morris, of Providence, R. I., I took exit from Philadelphia by way of the Camden and Amboy R. R., en route for N. Y.

articles.headline: To the Colored People of the United States
articles.author: Daniel A. Payne
articles.summary: Men, Brethren, Sisters: A crisis is upon us, which no one can enable us to meet, conquer, and convert into blessings for all concerned, but that God who builds up one nation and breaks down another. For more than one generation associations of white men, entitled Colonization Societies, have been engaged in plans and efforts for our expatriation... but now the American Government has assumed the work and responsibility of colonizing us in some foreign land within the torrid zone.

articles.headline: Home (editor's return; Philadelphia in wartime)
articles.summary: Through the ever-merciful providence of a kind and indulgent Father, we again find ourself at home, safe and sound... Business of every kind is dull now in Philadelphia. We find many of the business places shut up, and many of their occupants gone to the seat of war.

articles.summary: The second quarterly arrangements of the Norristown circuit; the quarterly conference at Zion Mission, Philadelphia, September 20, 1862, at 3 o'clock, P. M. Q'ly M'g, Sept. 21, Zion Mission, Phila.; Sept. 28, Norristown; Oct. 5, West Philadelphia; Oct. 12, Old Chester; Oct. 19, Horntown [VERIFY]; Oct. 26, Germantown; Nov. 2, The Chester [VERIFY]. W. D. W. Schureman, Elder in Charge. T. H. Cooper, Subordinate.

articles.headline: What We Are Doing in Burlington
articles.summary: Bro. Weaver: Our church seems to be in a prosperous condition, and in fact all the churches and Sabbath Schools on this circuit, under the supervision of Elder Smith, and Bro. J. H. Long, assistant. On the evening of the 10th inst. the young ladies and gentlemen surprised Bro. Long with a giving visit, at which time he was presented with Three dollars and twenty-eight cents in money, and more than double that amount in groceries and other donations. Signed A. C. S..
people: assistant preacher, Burlington circuit; recipient of donation visit Sept. 10

articles.headline: Bishop Payne (editorial note)
articles.summary: We call our readers' attention to a splendid article written by Bishop Payne in relation to the colored race in this country. Let every body read it.
people: Bishop; author of the article (printed 'Bishop Payne')

articles.headline: Mrs. Martha Collins, infant school (advertisement)
articles.summary: MRS. MARTHA COLLINS, 730 Russell Street, above Fitzwater. Begs leave to inform her friends and the public generally, that she has opened an INFANT SCHOOL, for Boys and Girls, to whom she will pay special attention in teaching the primary departments of Reading, Writing, and Arithmetic, also Singing, upon the most reasonable and accommodating terms. She does not hesitate to say that she will be able to please all who may give her a trial.
people: Mrs.; infant school for boys and girls, 730 Russell Street, above Fitzwater

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits (with notice of a Sabbath School Convention)
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: I have just paid a debt in visiting my western brethren and sisters, of the western portion of the A. M. E. Church, a debt that I was not aware was due. I rejoice to be favored with an opportunity of making payment.
people: preacher in charge, Freehold circuit (printed 'Brother W. Winder')

articles.headline: Mrs. Francis E. Watkins Harper on the War and the President's Colonization Scheme
articles.author: Francis E. Watkins Harper
articles.summary: Let me refer to the great topic of the day, the war. You ask my opinion, I think, in one of your letters. To me the times are gloomy, and though I stand not in the valley of vision, and my lips neither tremble nor thrill with the prophet's ecstasy or agony, yet if I can read the fate of this republic by the lurid light that gleams around the tombs of buried nations...

articles.headline: Appointments: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street
articles.summary: On Sunday, the 28th inst., at 10 A. M., in the Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street, a discourse will be delivered by the pastor. Theme, 'Seven Upward Steps.' In the evening, at 7 1/2 o'clock, a discourse entitled, 'Seven Downward Steps.'

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings: Bridgeton Circuit
articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meetings for Bridgeton Circuit. The Quarterly Conference at Back Neck, September 27th, 1862, at 10 o'clock, A. M. October 5th, at Springtown. 19th, at Gouldtown. 26th, at Bridgeton. Joshua Woodlin, Elder in charge.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Peter Gardiner, October 4-5)
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: My next Quarterly Meeting will be held on next Saturday and Sabbath, the 4th and 5th of October. Peter Gardiner, Preacher in charge.

articles.headline: The Proclamation of the President (editorial)
articles.summary: The proclamation of the President of the United States will be read with interest by all of our people, and all true lovers of freedom, irrespective of clime or caste, will give three hearty cheers for Abraham Lincoln, President of the United States of America. Now if every man would work and throw down prejudice, the country would soon be redeemed... and that is to let every body be free. Amen, Amen.

articles.headline: Things In and About Philadelphia
articles.summary: There is a sense of feeling in Philadelphia about the war. Many are looking with anxious hearts for the triumph and victory of General McClellan, and there are some, and no small number, too, for the success of Jeff Davis, and his men. Others are in favor of a universal emancipation, and putting down this rebellion by using all able bodied men; while others are saying there is a negro in the wood pile...

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Rev. H. Davis, for Jas. E. Hall, $1 00. Albert H. Hall, 1 00. Rev. A. Johnson, of Johnstown, Pa., for two subscribers at Richmond, Pa., 2 00. Miss Margt. Steward, of Bridgeton, N. J., 50. Rev. H. M. Turner, on account, 4 00. Mr. Daniel Davidson, of Alexandria, Va., 1 00.

articles.headline: Notice (editor to preach at Bethel for the contrabands)
articles.summary: We have received from two brethren a special request to preach for them out of the city on Sabbath. We would just say that a collection is to be taken up in Bethel Church on the following Sabbath for the contrabands, and Brother Campbell announced to his Board that we would preach for him at 3 o'clock on Sabbath, the 25th [sic; probably 28th] inst. On their account I stay to fill the appointment, to do all the good I can for suffering humanity.

articles.headline: Contrabands in Washington
articles.summary: We have read a letter from the President of the National Freedman's Society, of Washington, giving a graphic description of the condition of the poor, oppressed contrabands who are coming into Washington... There are about 2,500 there now... according to the letter which the President of the Society sent to our friend, Mr. Still, of this city. It calls upon the colored people of Philadelphia to aid our brethren in their suffering condition.
people: recipient of the National Freedman's Society letter (printed 'Mr. Still, of this city')

events.name: A.M.E. Union Church, Philadelphia -- quarterly conference and quarterly meeting announced
events.description: Notice signed H. Davis, Minister: the Quarterly Conference of the members of the Union Church to be held on the evening of July 18, and the Quarterly Meeting in the church on July 19 and 20, 1862.

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia -- quarterly meeting
events.description: Sabbath July 6, 1862: love feast 8-9 a.m.; preaching 10 1/2 a.m. (theme 'Christian in the World'); 3 p.m. preaching by Rev. E. Weaver and the Lord's Supper; 8 p.m. preaching (theme 'A Stone with Seven Eyes'). Notice signed A. L. Stanford, Minister. The July 12 issue (p2) reports that 'the Rev. A. L. Stanford's Quarterly Meeting came off finely last Sabbath. There was a good feeling all the day long.'

events.name: A.M.E. Church, New Brunswick, N.J. -- ladies' festival
events.location: A.M.E. Church, New Brunswick, N.J. (Princeton circuit, Philadelphia Conference)
events.description: Grand festival held by the ladies of the A.M.E. Church of New Brunswick on June 25, 1862; the Committee realized $53, of which some of the brethren thought $13 would cover expenses, leaving $40 profit. Reported in a letter signed for the Committee and Pastor by Wm. Offer [VERIFY] and Rev. Theodore Gould, dated Princeton, N.J., 'June 31' (sic), 1862. No committee members named.

events.name: A.M.E. Mission Sabbath School of Kaighnsville, N.J. -- pleasure trip
events.location: Maple Grove, near Diamond Cottage (Kaighnsville, N.J., Camden circuit)
events.description: Pleasure trip of the A.M.E. Mission Sabbath School of Kaighnsville, N.J., under the charge of Rev. Peter Gardiner of the Camden circuit, Thursday July 24, 1862, at Maple Grove near Diamond Cottage. Addresses by Rev. Peter Gardiner, Rev. Elisha Weaver and others; the July 19 reprint adds that Rev. W. D. W. Scheroman (as printed; = W. D. W. Schureman) will speak. Committee of Arrangements: Jacob F. Dennison [VERIFY], Henry Mackey [VERIFY], Henry Harrison [VERIFY]. 'All other usual business and work will necessarily be postponed for two weeks.'
attendees: speaker (Rev.; printed 'Scheroman' in the July 19 reprint)

events.name: A.M.E. Church, Frankford -- quarterly meeting
events.description: Editorial report (by the editor, Weaver) of a quarterly meeting at Frankford with 'Father Roberson' (headed 'Rev. R. Roberson'): the church, yard and part of the street crowded, the largest the editor had seen there. Love feast early in the morning; at 11 o'clock Father Marys [VERIFY], a local deacon, preached, followed by three or four short exhortations; at 3 o'clock the editor preached and consecrated the Sacrament. Date not stated (between July 12 and 19, presumably Sunday July 13).

events.name: Burlington A.M.E. Sabbath School -- Sabbath School walk
events.description: Notice that the Burlington Sabbath School walk will take place on July 17, 1862, signed J. H. Smith, Elder, and J. H. Long [VERIFY], Pastor.

events.name: A. M. E. Mission School Walk (postponed)
events.description: Editorial notice: the A. M. E. Mission School Walk, earlier postponed, to take place on the 7th inst.; the editor hopes the mission school will be encouraged. No officers named.

events.name: Bordentown circuit bush meeting
events.description: Bush (camp) meeting of the Bordentown circuit, Philadelphia Conference, under Rev. H. Young, elder in charge, Aug. 10 to 17, 1862, at Cookstown, N. J.; the public invited.

events.name: Ladies' G. McMullen Sewing Circle -- Harvest Home
events.location: Moses' Woods, Trenton, N. J.; festival in the church at night
events.description: The Ladies' G. McMullen Sewing Circle of the A. M. E. Mount Zion Church, Trenton (pastor Rev. William Moore), held a Harvest Home for the benefit of the organization: a grand dinner on the ground, refreshments, addresses by eminent speakers, and a festival in the church at night. Trenton is a Philadelphia Conference station. The 'From the Churches' column the same day reports 'Rev. Elder Moore, pastor of the Trenton Church' visiting the book-room on Tuesday and attending the preachers' meeting.

events.name: Bethel Church (Philadelphia) -- quarterly meeting
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting of Bethel Church under Rev. J. P. Campbell, opening on the 25th ult. with a general class; preaching Saturday night; on the Sabbath (July 27) at ten o'clock Rev. Henry Davis preached; at three o'clock 'we preached for Elder Campbell' (as printed); at night Rev. J. R. V. Morgan; love feast on Monday night (July 28). The editor adds that a severe attack of indisposition kept him at home.

events.name: Burlington A. M. E. Church -- benefit dinner in the Fountain Woods
events.location: Fountain Woods, one mile from Burlington, N. J.; carriages from the church in Pearl Street
events.description: Benefit dinner for the A. M. E. Church in Burlington, N. J., tickets 25 cents, carriages leaving the church in Pearl Street for the ground. Signed J. H. Smith, Elder, and J. H. Long, Minister. The same page carries a second Burlington circuit notice (dated August 1st, 1862) announcing the grand celebration of the Sabbath schools of the Burlington circuit on the 28th of August at Snow Hill, signed J. H. Smith, Elder, and 'H. J. Long', Pastor.

events.name: Burlington circuit -- grand Sabbath-school celebration
events.description: Grand celebration of the Sabbath schools of the Burlington circuit (Philadelphia Conference) on the 28th of August at Snow Hill; announced by J. H. Smith, Elder, and H. J. Long, Pastor, in a notice dated August 1st, 1862.

events.name: Sacrament of the Lord, Brick Wesley Church (A. M. E. Zion)
events.description: Sabbath Aug. 10, 1862: at 11 a.m. the pastor of Brick Wesley Church to preach; at 3 p.m. Rev. Elisha Weaver, A. M. E. editor, to preach a sacramental discourse, followed by the Lord's Supper. Signed John A. Williams, Minister in Charge. (A letter from Carlisle, Pa., on the same page, col. 3, names 'Rev. John A. Williams, pastor of Wesley Zion Church, of Philadelphia', who preached at Harrisburg at the first quarterly meeting, June 29-30.) A notable A. M. E. / A. M. E. Zion pulpit exchange.
attendees: minister in charge (pastor of Wesley Zion Church, Philadelphia, per the Carlisle letter)

events.name: Bethel Sunday School -- resolutions on the death of librarian Henry Downing
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Meeting of the teachers and scholars of Bethel Sunday School announced the death of their librarian Henry Downing and named Joseph Brister, Daniel T. Masten and Mrs. Armstrong a committee to draft resolutions of condolence: the Association has lost an efficient member and the School an excellent librarian; the resolutions to be sent to the family; the Association to attend the funeral in a body; resolutions to be published in the Recorder. Signed Daniel T. Masten, Secretary of the Committee, Philadelphia, August 2d, 1862.

events.name: Camden circuit bush meeting
events.location: Heinesville [VERIFY: printed 'Heiseaville' or similar], Camden, N. J.
events.description: Bush meeting of the Camden circuit (Philadelphia Conference), Peter Gardiner, preacher in charge, to begin Thursday Aug. 21, 1862, at 3 p.m., for a few days; Revs. J. P. Campbell, A. L. Stanford, H. Davis and E. Weaver expected to assist. N. B.: no stands or tents to sell anything on the ground except two boarding tents. Committee: Messrs. J. F. Derrickson, H. Mackey [VERIFY], J. Wright, H. H. Harrison [VERIFY] and Elihu [VERIFY] Jefferson. Dated August 14th, 1862 (year printed '1865' in error on the film).

events.name: Editor Weaver calls on ex-President Roberts of Liberia at the Continental Hotel
events.description: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, first President of Liberia ('Ex-President Roberts'; given names not printed), on a short visit to the United States with his wife, stayed at the Continental (Hotel), Philadelphia. Elisha Weaver called on him Saturday Aug. 9, 1862, and describes him as a scholar and gentleman of refinement, of medium size, his face 'resembling that of a Frenchman': 'Our interview with him made us feel proud to have the honor of calling on the first President that Liberia ever acknowledged.'

events.name: Funeral eulogy for Hannah Vandyke, Norristown A. M. E. Church
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Norristown, Pa.
events.description: Rev. Henry Davis delivered a eulogy (text Revelation 14:13) on Hannah Vandyke, late consort of Henry Vandyke, residing near Norristown. Born in New Jersey in 1810 [VERIFY], she lived there two years, moved with her parents to Berks County and thence to Plymouth, Montgomery County; married Henry Vandyke in 1828 [VERIFY]; embraced religion and joined the A. M. E. Church in Norristown in 1830 [VERIFY], remaining an honourable member until her death; 'an industrious, affectionate and an obedient wife... a loving and indulgent mother... a kind neighbor, a civil citizen'. Taken ill in December 1861, she died May 11th, 1862. Signed Henry Davis. Date of the eulogy not stated.

events.name: Wesley A. M. E. Sabbath School -- twenty-second anniversary excursion
events.location: Washington Retreat (cars from Fifteenth and Willow Sts., Philadelphia)
events.description: Twenty-second anniversary of the A. M. E. Wesley Sabbath School (pastor Rev. A. L. Stanford; superintendent Mr. J. H. Hughes) at the Washington Retreat, Thursday Sept. 4, 1862; several distinguished ministers expected. Cars from Fifteenth and Willow Sts. at 8, 10, 9.30 [sic], 10.30, 11.30 a.m. and 2, 3.15, 4.15 p.m. Excursion tickets (adults 20 cents, children 15 cents [VERIFY: '15' or '16']) of the Superintendent, 805 [VERIFY] Montcalm Street; of Mrs. E. Nixon, 742 Lombard Street; or at the Pastorate, No. 247 Currant Alley, above Spruce St.
attendees: pastor (Rev.); pastorate No. 247 Currant Alley, above Spruce St.

events.name: United Benevolent Daughters of Rev. Henry Davis' Society -- address by Rev. J. P. Campbell
events.location: A. M. E. Church, Frankford, Pa.
events.description: Rev. Jabez B. [sic] Campbell to address the members of the United Benevolent Daughters of Rev. Henry Davis' Society in the A. M. E. Church, Frankford, evening of Sept. 4, 1862; doors 7.30; admittance ten cents; proceeds and the profits of refreshments for the Society. Officers: Letitia Bowzar, President; Elizabeth Morris [VERIFY], Secretary.

events.name: Norristown circuit -- Sabbath-school anniversary
events.location: Mr. Ashur's [?] Woods, about a mile and a half from Horntown [?], Pa.
events.description: Several Sabbath schools of the Norristown circuit (Philadelphia Conference) to celebrate their anniversary on Wednesday, Sept. 3, 1862, in the woods named; eminent speakers expected. Signed W. D. W. Schureman, Elder in charge (printed 'Schureman'), and T. H. Cooper, Subordinate. The same column reports Schureman 'recovering as fast as the circumstances of his case will allow' after his Aug. 7 injury, which happened at 'Horntown [?]' (Aug. 16 issue).

events.name: Zion Wesleyan M. E. Church (Big Wesley) -- camp meeting at Judge Peters' Farm
events.location: Judge Peters' Farm, near Philadelphia (cars from 15th and Willow streets)
events.description: Notice (signed John A. Williams, Minister in Charge) and report (signed 'St. Cyprian'). The camp meeting of the Zion Wesleyan M. E. church ('Big Wesley'), Rev. John A. Williams, pastor, began Friday, Aug. 29 and was to continue until Tuesday, Sept. 9. The notice announced that Revs. A. L. Stanford, J. P. Campbell, 'Rev. Bishop Rees' [VERIFY] and others would preach on Sabbath, Sept. 7; cars leave 15th and Willow streets at 8 o'clock A.M. and every hour; excursion tickets reduced to 12 cents. The report describes Sabbath, Aug. 31: morning sermon by Rev. H. A. Gibson [VERIFY] (Matt. 9th and 12th), afternoon sermon by 'the Rt. Rev. John Ross' [VERIFY] (Mark viii. 38), evening sermon by Rev. T. J. Riddle [VERIFY] (Exodus xxxiii. 14). An efficient police force was on the ground; many 'of our people apprehended difficulty and bloodshed' because the meeting was held so near the city and some invited interference from 'the less considerate of our white population', yet not the slightest disorder occurred.
attendees: pastor and minister in charge, Zion Wesleyan M. E. Church ('Big Wesley') (Rev.)

events.name: Bethel Church -- called meeting of male members on the employment of colored men as soldiers
events.description: At a called meeting of the male members and congregation of the African Methodist Episcopal Church, held in the Bethel meeting-house, Rev. Jabez P. Campbell was called to the chair and Lewis R. Seymour appointed Secretary; the object was 'to state our own position in the present crisis upon the country'. Preamble: the people of the United States hold that it will 'degrade the whites to fight by the side of the negro'; 'in no case, at the present, will the negroes be armed or employed as soldiers'; certain 'restless spirits among our people in this city', part of the floating population, press themselves on the authorities as representatives of the colored people of Philadelphia and Pennsylvania, 'with the assumption that they desire to thrust themselves on the Government as soldiers, unasked or unsolicited'. Resolved: that 'the better class of colored people have too much self-respect to intrude themselves where they are not wanted'; that persons representing otherwise do not represent the colored people and act without authority; that the colored people of Philadelphia, a loyal and peace-loving community, desire by no act of theirs to increase disorder. Rev. J. P. Campbell, L. R. Seymour and Abraham Field were named a committee to publish the resolutions in the daily and weekly papers. Signed Rev. J. P. Campbell, President; L. R. Seymour, Secretary. Undated; printed Sept. 6, 1862, i.e. on the eve of the Antietam-campaign emergency.
attendees: chairman/president (Rev.; printed 'Jabez P. Campbell' and 'J. P. Campbell'); publication committee
secretary (also printed 'L. R. Seymour'); publication committee

events.name: Union Sons and Daughters of Hensoe [VERIFY] Society, Bensalem -- second anniversary
events.location: Bensalem, Bucks County, Pa. (woods of Mr. George Pickering)
events.description: Report signed 'Hopeful'. The Union Sons and Daughters of Hensoe [VERIFY: society name] Society, located in Bensalem, Bucks county, held their second anniversary August 21: the members in uniform of 'Red, White and Blue' marched in procession to the woods of Mr. George Pickering, where a large concourse had gathered, and were addressed by 'the very Rev. H. Davis, of Frankford'. The society is in the fifth year of its existence, formed to assist members in sickness and death. Motto: 'Justice to all that join the Sons and Daughters of Temperance.' No officers named.

events.name: Burlington circuit -- donation visit to Bro. J. H. Long
events.description: Letter signed A. C. S. On the evening of Sept. 10 the young ladies and gentlemen of the Burlington church surprised Bro. J. H. Long, assistant to 'Elder Smith' (presumably J. H. Smith, Elder of the Burlington circuit, see Sept. 6 notice), with a 'giving visit': $3.28 in money and more than double that in groceries. Bro. Smith returned thanks; 'Bro. Stevens' made the presentation, presenting a book recommended by Conference, and noted that the members had some months ago organized an Aid Society meeting monthly for the benefit of Elder Smith, plus fifty cents from an absent gentleman.

events.name: Sabbath School Convention of the Philadelphia District -- called by Bishop Nazrey
events.description: In a postscript to his 'Episcopal Visits' letter, Bishop Willis Nazrey recalls the resolution of the Philadelphia Annual Conference held in Trenton, New Jersey, 1862: 'That we recommend to this conference, that it would be highly important for a Sabbath School Convention, to be held in the Philadelphia District, consisting of the Bishop, or Bishops, Ministers having charge, Superintendents, Teachers, and delegates not exceeding two from each circuit or station, and that the Bishop be requested to appoint the time and place of holding said convention.' He gives notice that the convention will be held in Bethel Church, Sixth St., on Wednesday, the 12th of November, 1862. Another postscript asks Brother W. Winder, preacher in charge of Freehold circuit, to write to him at Providence, Oct. 10-14.

events.name: Norristown circuit second quarterly meeting at Zion Mission; Camden quarterly meeting
events.description: Editor's report: 'Last Sabbath' (Sept. 21) the Rev. W. D. W. Schureman held his Second Quarterly Meeting for the Norristown circuit in Zion Mission, Philadelphia; love feast early in the morning; at 11 o'clock 'Brother Burly' preached, 'one of the young man's best efforts'. In the afternoon the editor crossed to Camden, N.J., to the Quarterly Meeting of Rev. Peter Gardiner and heard him preach; at night he preached for the congregation of Rev. A. L. Stanford, as Bro. Stanford preached for Bro. Gardiner at eight. 'The house was crowded from the stairs close up to the altar.' The Methodist, Presbyterian, Baptist and Episcopalian churches 'are all getting along pretty well.'

events.name: Bethel Church -- meeting for the relief of the contrabands in Washington; relief committee of seven
events.description: On 'last Tuesday night' (Sept. 23) a meeting was held at Bethel Church, called by the pastor Rev. J. P. Campbell, to consider the urgent call for aid from the National Freedman's Society of Washington (whose president had written to Mr. Still); the S. C. Statistical Association of the State of Pennsylvania had already sent letters to the ministers and churches. Rev. J. P. Campbell was appointed Chairman and Mr. R. L. Seymour Secretary. Rev. Elisha Weaver, Rev. Stephen Smith and Bro. Abraham Field were the business committee and brought in a preamble and resolutions to raise money forthwith and to take up a collection through the day on Sabbath in Bethel Church. Mr. E. M. Thomas, a citizen of Washington, gave an eye-witness statement and received a vote of thanks. A committee of seven (three males and four females) was appointed, to whom goods and money were to be sent, at these addresses as printed: Rev. J. P. Campbell, No. 882 [VERIFY: or 832] Carpenter St.; Rev. Stephen Smith, No. 921 Lombard St.; Mr. Morris Hall, No. 1022 Lombard St.; Mrs. Jane Johnson, No. 618 South St.; Mrs. Mary C. Weaver, No. 619 Pine St.; Mrs. Mary L. Jones, No. 919 South St. (printed 'Mary S. Jones' in the minutes and 'Mary L. Jones' in the address list) [VERIFY]; Miss Esther Armstrong, No. 704 [VERIFY] Lebanon St. (In the minutes the males are 'Rev. J. P. Campbell, Rev. S. Smith, and Brother Hall'.) The proceedings and the committee's names and addresses were ordered published in the Recorder until recalled. A collection of $35.50 was taken at the meeting, some paying $5 and some $1. Adjourned subject to the call of the chairman.
attendees: pastor of Bethel; chairman and relief committee (Rev.), No. 882 [VERIFY] Carpenter St.
secretary (printed 'R. L. Seymour'; probably the L. R. Seymour of Sept. 6)
business committee; relief committee (Rev.), No. 921 Lombard St.
